system_note: Reviewed readmission RM_06 (admit 06/26/2026, gap_days=6) against index MR_06 (discharge 06/20/2026). Great Basin Preferred Care's guideline specifies a 30-day review window ("30 days from prior discharge") so this readmission is in-scope (Policy doc citation: Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Great Basin Preferred Care - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, position 4). The medical record documents the readmission diagnosis as an infected pancreatic pseudocyst and explicitly states this is a direct late complication of the index necrotizing pancreatitis: "Clinical Relationship: Index admission MR_06 (03/02-06/20/2026): Necrotizing gallstone pancreatitis (K85.12) with 40-50% necrosis; step-up drainage and VARD performed; cholecystectomy for biliary etiology. Readmission RM_06 (06/26-07/08/2026): Infected pancreatic pseudocyst (K86.3) with infected necrosis (K85.12) - direct late complication of the index necrotizing pancreatitis. Both admissions share K85.12 as a coded diagnosis." (DISCHARGE SUMMARY, Transfer / Discharge Summary › Discharge / Transfer Summary, pp. 139-140). Procedural/pathology support for infection is present: "CT-guided aspiration performed of the pancreatic bed. Purulent material obtained. Gram stain and cultures sent. Confirmatory infection." (Pancreatic Necrosis, Chart Notes, p. 73). The payer guideline's relatedness criteria include both "same or clinically related condition" and "new infection/complication arising from care provided during the prior stay" and require documentation linking the readmission to the index stay; the record meets these criteria (Policy doc citations: positions 12 and 13). The guideline's exclusions (e.g. direct transfers, scheduled admissions, burn, newborn/obstetric, transplant, inpatient behavioral health, admissions to SNF/LTACH/IRF) would override a Finding, but no exclusion applies in this case (Policy Documents/Readmission/Payer Guidelines/Great Basin Preferred Care - Readmission Review Guideline.docx, position 21). Conclusion: the record supports that RM_06 is clinically related to MR_06 and qualifies as a Finding under the payer's readmission guideline (Finding Reason: infection/complication of care related to prior necrotizing pancreatitis). Evidence used: payer guideline (positions 4, 12, 13, 21), the discharge summary clinical relationship statement (pp. 139-140), and CT-guided aspiration note confirming purulent material (p. 73).
rationale_letter: Re: Readmission review - RM_06 (admit 06/26/2026) to Great Basin Preferred Care We completed a clinical readmission review of inpatient claim RM_06 and the paired index claim MR_06. Per Great Basin Preferred Care's Readmission Review Guideline (review window: 30 days from prior discharge), this readmission (6 days after the index discharge) is within the review window and subject to review. The documentation shows that the patient was readmitted with an infected pancreatic pseudocyst (K86.3) and infected necrosis. The hospital discharge summary explicitly states that the readmission was a "direct late complication of the index necrotizing pancreatitis" (index dx K85.12), and interventional radiology confirmed purulent material from the pancreatic bed on CT-guided aspiration. Under the payer's guideline the readmission therefore meets the criterion for an infection/complication arising from the care provided during the prior stay and is clinically related to the index admission. Finding: The readmission RM_06 is a Finding under Great Basin Preferred Care's readmission policy - specifically, it meets the "infection or complication of care" criterion because the infected pancreatic pseudocyst and infected necrosis are documented as a direct complication of the index necrotizing pancreatitis (MR_06). Correction: This readmission will be processed as clinically related to the index stay per the payer's readmission policy. If you disagree with this determination, please provide additional clinical documentation showing that the readmission was unrelated (for example, evidence that the pseudocyst infection arose from a new, unrelated event or that an applicable exclusion applies). Sincerely, Clinical Claims Auditor
